clue.text: Denied turn to a little boy and became base

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Denied turn to a little boy and became base' cannot give DEGENERATED: the wordplay needs RENEGADE (anagram to DEGENERA) + TED, so 'Denied' looks like a misread of 'Renegade', more than three letters off, and no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: Denied turn to a little boy and became base

clue.text: Point to agent in sight

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Someone points a secret agent out to a watcher who has them in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between the wordplay and the definition, which is 'sight' used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sight something is to catch a glimpse of it, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Where big lake is rising?

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word for the lake is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A geography question asking where a large lake's water level is going up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'is rising' turns ERIE upwards; the whole clue also asks for a place, the Irish state's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish name for Ireland is a place, which answers the question where.

clue.text: Competitors making records

explanation.surface: Rivals in a contest are setting new records.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitors in a contest are its entrants, and items written into a log or register are its records.

clue.text: They're used for cutting spindles

explanation.surface: A note that spindles are tools for cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatchets are chopping tools, and spindles are shafts things rotate on, plural of axis.

clue.text: Eeyore's upset by blemish

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters of the donkey's name are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh's gloomy donkey is distressed by a mark on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like Eeyore's mood but is the anagram signal; the possessive S counts as a letter here. 'by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly building or sight that spoils a view is a blot on the landscape, a blemish.

clue.text: One on the board making plans

explanation.surface: A board member who is busy drawing up plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece in the game of checkers sits on the board, and a technical drawer makes plans for buildings and machines.

clue.text: Clip-joint?

parts.note: a clip joint is slang for a venue that overcharges, but read literally it is a place where hair is clipped

explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser's for men is where customers get their hair clipped.

clue.text: Time to return to a region

indicators.note: to return asks for the word for a period of time to be read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone longs to go back in time to a particular part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns ERA round; the second 'to' merely joins it to A.
explanation.definitionFit: A district or zone is a region, a synonym.

clue.text: Flat-finding agency

parts.note: reads like a firm that finds homes to rent, but means a tool that finds whether a surface is level

explanation.definitionFit: A builder's tool with a bubble in a liquid tube shows whether a surface is horizontal.

clue.text: It throws light on a possible bloomer

explanation.surface: Something that sheds light on a likely blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric lamp gives off light, and a tulip or daffodil starts as a rounded root that may flower.

clue.text: Admit the account needs information

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that the bookkeeping requires more facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to own up to it or recognise it, a synonym.

clue.text: The concept of absent-mindedness

explanation.surface: A discussion of the idea of forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: A general idea apart from concrete things is an abstract notion, and a dreamy, preoccupied state is also called this.

clue.text: The last person to be a snob

explanation.surface: A remark that the final person is a snob.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker works on, and 'snob' is an old dialect word for a shoemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe mender works on a last, and snob is an old name for a shoe mender.

clue.text: Was angry getting a bad grade

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of the word grade are spoiled into another order

explanation.surface: A student was furious at getting a poor mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' looks like it describes the grade but is the anagram signal; 'getting a' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging is being furious, so the past tense means was angry.

clue.text: A relative right in the midst of trouble

indicators.note: in the midst of puts the letter for right inside the word for trouble

explanation.surface: A family member has got caught up in some difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A male sibling is a relative.

clue.text: Short and direct

explanation.surface: An instruction to be short and straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief means concise or short, and to brief someone is to instruct or direct them.

clue.text: Bears disguised weapon

indicators.note: disguised says the letters of the word bears are dressed up in another order

explanation.surface: Bears in fancy dress are carrying a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' is the anagram signal: BEARS rearranges to the sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry sword with a curved blade is a weapon.

clue.text: Where cricketers practise catches

explanation.surface: The spot where cricketers practise taking catches.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket nets are netted practice lanes where batsmen and bowlers train.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers train in netted lanes, and to catch a fish is to land it in a mesh.

clue.text: One vessel accommodates one rowing crew

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: accommodates means the ship's letters take the second numeral inside them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single boat has room for an oarsman from a rowing team.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is Oxford University's reserve eight, named after the stretch of the Thames at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford's second boat in the Boat Race is named after the city's river.

clue.text: Course must be if you steer wrongly

definitions.text: Course must be if you steer wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of the word steer are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A navigator's rule: after a steering error, the heading must be put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' is the anagram signal on STEER; read whole, the clue says a bad steer means the course must be fixed again.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a course again after an error is to correct the heading.

clue.text: Cotton on a reel is in a tangle

indicators.note: in a tangle says the letters of these words are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: Thread wound on a spool has got knotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton on' looks like thread on a reel, but it is the British phrase for understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is a British idiom for grasping or understanding something.

clue.text: Admitted being deceived?

explanation.surface: Someone who was let in had in fact been fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone allowed into a place is let in, and someone fooled or conned is hoodwinked.

clue.text: Gave a caning-exhausted!

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster who handed out a beating was worn out afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To whack is to strike hard, and whacked is informal for tired out.

clue.text: A medley of jazz music in Portuguese resort

indicators.note: in places the music word inside the resort's name

parts.note: Faro is a resort town on Portugal's Algarve coast
rag, short for ragtime, is an early jazz style

explanation.surface: A mix of jazz tunes playing in a holiday town on the Algarve.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused jumble or mixture is a medley, a synonym.

clue.text: Dines in style at smart restaurants

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Someone takes meals in fine fashion at fancy restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'stylE AT Smart'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to have a meal, and eats is the plain verb for that.

clue.text: Riding-establishment boss

explanation.surface: The manager of a riding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeding farm for horses is a horse establishment, and a stud is also a knob or raised fastener.

clue.text: What some of the best artistes do

definitions.text: What some of the best artistes do

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a part of the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: A remark on what certain top performers achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'beST ARtistes'; read whole, the clue says what top performers do: take the lead role.
explanation.definitionFit: Top performers headline a show, taking the leading role.

clue.text: First ride on a new horse

indicators.note: First asks for the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Someone takes a first ride on an unfamiliar horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse with a coat of mixed white and coloured hairs.

clue.text: Honour saint at home, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in puts the saint and home letters inside the word for speech style

parts.note: diction is a manner of speaking or enunciation

explanation.surface: A saint is honoured at home in a particular way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like the idiom for so to speak, but 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An award or mark of excellence is an honour.

clue.text: Continue being visibly a stupid person

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on being plainly an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visibly' says the second meaning holds when the two words are written as one.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to proceed, and a buffoon or idiot is a stupid person.

clue.text: Special band for the match

parts.note: reads like a group playing at a game, but a match is a marriage and the band is worn on a finger

explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a match, and the ring given at it is a circular band.
